stories.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
summary: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally.

University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia.
Keeping regular times for sleeping, eating, and other activities may help regulate the body's internal clock, which influences mood, sleep, and overall health.

stories.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
summary: Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers.
The same patterns also reveal which brains are unusually resistant to aging, raising hopes for future treatments that could help protect memory.

stories.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
summary: Astronomers have uncovered a potentially enormous new dwarf planet beyond Pluto, hidden for years in one of the most crowded regions of the night sky.
The discovery of 2026 ED138 could expand the solar system's official dwarf planet family and hints that more mysterious worlds may be lurking far beyond Neptune.

stories.title: How to spot November's planetary parade in the pre-dawn sky
summary: The planets of Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter will align in pre-dawn sky throughout November.

stories.title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets
summary: Gardeners across Sussex are changing their planting strategies after this year's unprecedented heat.

stories.title: Bluetongue virus confirmed on County Down farm
summary: Officials from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs said the virus had been detected in three sheep.

stories.title: 5,000-year-old skulls reveal a disturbing secret of ancient Egypt's first kings
summary: A 5,000-year-old mystery surrounding the tombs of Egypt’s first kings has taken a disturbing turn.
Scientists reexamining 46 ancient skulls discovered evidence of potentially fatal head injuries in 18, suggesting that at least 39% of those studied may have been deliberately killed.
The findings support a century-old theory that royal attendants were sacrificed when kings died, possibly to serve them in the afterlife.

stories.title: Scientists capture electrons making seemingly impossible quantum jumps
summary: Scientists have captured electrons making seemingly impossible jumps across forbidden energy gaps in graphene, with some transitions occurring at a remarkable 100% probability.
The breakthrough offers an unprecedented look at quantum behavior and could help unlock a new generation of ultrafast, light-controlled electronics.

stories.title: What could El Niño mean for winter weather in the US and Canada?
summary: El Niño winters typically bring more rain in the southern USA and drier, warmer conditions further north but the impacts on snowfall are complex.

stories.title: Climate action discussed at youth COP meeting
summary: School children gather to discuss climate issues to coincide with the COP31 conference in Turkey.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent
summary: A new study reveals that viral infections may leave behind hidden damage to the immune system long after symptoms disappear.
Researchers found that mice recovering from an acute infection experienced lasting changes to their spleens and weakened immune responses, potentially leaving them more vulnerable to future threats.
Surprisingly, prior vaccination completely prevented these harmful changes in the mouse model.

stories.title: Summer heatwave put bin crews lives at risk, says council worker
summary: Crews faced a "perfect storm" of challenges during the UK's record-breaking weather, it's claimed.

stories.title: Superheated magma could fuel towering lava fountains
summary: Why do some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly?
Scientists have discovered that a hidden effect of extreme heat inside magma may help explain the difference.
Experiments revealed that superheated magma can delay crystal formation for more than eight hours, compared with just 20 minutes in magma that has not been superheated.

stories.title: Dark energy may have flipped from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago
summary: A mysterious force driving the expansion of the Universe may have undergone a dramatic reversal billions of years ago.

Scientists exploring an overlooked branch of an alternative gravity theory discovered that dark energy could have switched from negative to positive roughly 9.5 billion years ago, potentially changing how we understand cosmic history.

stories.title: The Sun unleashed a monster storm. Earth may have made it worse
summary: The massive solar storm that illuminated skies worldwide in May 2024 has uncovered an unexpected twist: Earth's own atmosphere may have helped make the storm so powerful.
Satellite measurements revealed that roughly 85% of the charged particles fueling the disturbance originated from Earth's upper atmosphere rather than the solar wind.
Scientists also detected an extraordinary 40% weakening of Earth's magnetic field high above the planet.
